source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, banana cultivation techniques manual, 2019, section V.2.3 (banana leaf-roller / skipper caterpillar)
text:
The banana leaf-roller (banana skipper), Erionota thrax (cited in the source as Erionota thrase), is a large brown moth/skipper with white-spotted wings whose larvae cause serious leaf damage, especially during the humid rainy season around October-November. Females lay eggs in small clusters of 2-3 on the underside of leaves near the edges; eggs hatch in about 4-5 days into white, brown-headed larvae that roll the leaf edge into a tube-like shelter and feed on the leaf tissue from inside it, a distinctive and easily recognized sign of this pest. The full life cycle from egg to adult is roughly 23-25 days, and because generations overlap, populations can build up quickly under favorable humid conditions.

Heavy infestation can strip large amounts of leaf area, reducing photosynthesis and weakening the plant, which lowers both yield and fruit quality.

Prevention and control: hand-collect and destroy rolled leaf sections containing larvae; where infestation is heavy, apply chlorpyrifos insecticide following label directions; and conserve natural enemies where present, since parasitic wasps in the families Ichneumonidae, Braconidae, and Chalcididae naturally attack the eggs, larvae, and pupae of this pest and can help keep populations in check without chemical intervention.
